comment: Ported: testbed pendulum_swingup is environment/ph_sac/dmc/pendulum.py with its factory in common/ph_dmc/pendulum.py; the row builds, its task_* columns are checked against the factory, and tests/test_ph_dmc_*.py compare the port with dm_control (forward dynamics, reset law and open-loop trajectories, and the reward at margin 0 against dm_control's get_reward; the row's margin-2 reward is tested against dm_control's rewards.tolerance). Task values from docs/dmc_environments/dmc_environments.tex and docs/paper/sections/E_experiment_details.tex. dm_control pendulum/swingup: one hinge, massless 0.5 m pole with a 1 kg bob (radius 0.05 m), damping 0.1, g 9.81; motor gear 1, torque +-1 N m. 1 ms RK4 physics as the cart-pole port (dm_control: 20 ms); fixed clock at dm_control's 20 ms control step (the reference period), 1000 decisions per 20 s episode. Reset: angle uniform on [-pi, pi), velocity 0. Reward dense since 2026-11-09, so NOT dm_control's pendulum/swingup reward: tol(cos theta; [cos 8 deg, 1], margin 2) with dm_control's default gaussian shape (value 0.1 at the margin) where dm_control sets margin 0, the form of dm_control's own dense tolerance rewards (acrobot/swingup is acrobot/swingup_sparse's bounds with margin 1), so no new code path. It is 1 within 8 deg of upright, 0.569 with the pole horizontal and 0.102 hanging (the margin spans the whole range of cos theta, so the reward falls to about the value at the margin at the bottom). dm_control's margin 0 (the indicator cos(theta) >= cos 8 deg) taught no arm anything in 500k decisions: with the 1 N m motor against 4.9 N m of gravity torque, a swing-up needs about 6.6 s of coherent pumping, random exploration gains 1-3% of the energy needed, and in 14,600 training episodes none entered the window from beyond 30 deg, so the value stayed flat outside the upright basin (the learned reward and plant were accurate). The reward still lies in [0, 1], so the sigmoid reward head (unit_interval_bounds) stays valid. The row remains dm_control's plant, motor, reset, clock and evaluation; its scores do not compare with published dm_control pendulum/swingup returns. No stop, no failure set. Decision box scaled to the motor: setpoint within +-3.14159 rad, stiffness 0-3.1831 N m/rad, damping 0-0.63662 N m s/rad (k_max = 10 x 1 N m / 3.14159 rad, damping 0.2 s x k_max, the rule that gives the cart-pole and Acrobot reference boxes at their +-10 limit); the setpoint is absolute with a wrapped error, as the windy swing-up's, which is how the companion document's 'decision box as the windy pendulum's' reads for a swing-up; flagged as a choice. The port reads the bob's inertia from dm_control's compiled model. Method and protocol columns as cartpole-swingup (cartpole_swingup.json) but the model step, the model integrator and the contact scheme's coarse step: K 400, tau 1 s, N 4, rate/actor steps 200/40, drift-only plant (diffusion none: the task is deterministic) integrated by the simulator's own step (model integrator rk4 on the RK4 rows, semi_implicit, MuJoCo's Euler step, on the swimmers' Euler), learned reward, always-admit, warm steps 2000/2000, leading_order, alpha_c tuned from 0.1 /s every 40 rows, 10 seeds, evaluation every 20k decisions on reset seeds 20000-20031; damping_rank is the velocity dimension as there, and the target entropy is decision_box_entropy_target of this row's box. Discount rate 0.5 /s as the swing-up tasks (dm_control and the paper set none). Feedback law evaluated at every RK4 stage, once per physics step at its start under Euler (task_refresh_mode continuous, since 2026-11-09; the runs before held it through each physics step) and terminal payoff 0 (failure_rate 0) as cartpole-swingup. Budget 500k decisions, the same number of decisions as cartpole-swingup (500 episodes of 1000 decisions; at 20 ms per decision this is 10000 s of interaction against the 10-s tasks' 5000 s). Model step 10 ms (2 substeps per 20 ms decision): common.ph_config.MODEL_STEPS, the largest step tried that divides the interval at which the oracle plant's one-interval model endpoint stays within 1e-3 relative error of the simulator's (99th percentile, decisions uniform in the box; 2026-11-09). Plant-step schedule (confirmed 2026-11-11): the learned plant takes its online step on every row until 100000 decisions, then on every k-th row, k = 4 (training plant_step_dense_until, plant_step_every; make_ct_ph_sac_table.PLANT_STEP_SCHEDULE).

Row of mode irregular: the final run's clock (decided 2026-11-11; on a fixed clock at the reference period the CT-SAC baseline is exactly SAC). The top row pendulum-swingup on an irregular clock, selected with --env-id pendulum-swingup --mode irregular; every column equals the top row's but env_clock_kind, env_tail_probability, env_tail_split, task_clock_kind, task_min_duration, task_max_duration and protocol_output_directory. Clock: the CT-SAC benchmark's irregular law (Nguyen 2026, arXiv:2602.14587, App. B.1.3 Table 1; environment/base.py sample_dt_from_distribution, two_tail_uniform with tail_p=0.99;tail_split=0.9 as benchmarks/hyperparams/ct_sac.csv's irregular rows): a whole number of 1 ms physics steps, 4 ms with probability 0.891, 60 ms with 0.099, and uniform on the 55 steps between with 0.010; the bounds T/5 and 3T of CT-SAC's cheetah-run and walker-run (common.ph_dmc._common.irregular_clock_bounds), T the reference period, 20 ms (dm_control's control step and CT-SAC's dt_default, unchanged). Mean interval 9.824 ms = 0.4912 T, so about 2036 decisions per 20 s episode (the top row: 1000), and the budget, in decisions as in the top row, covers 0.4912 times its simulated time (the evaluation cadence is in decisions too; the last interval of an episode is shortened at the time limit). A CHOICE: CT-SAC's quadruped-run used T/4 and 2.5T, humanoid-walk 0.4T and 1.6T with tail_p 0.8, tail_split 0.5. The model step need not divide an interval: an interval of n physics steps is integrated in ceil(n delta / h) equal substeps of at most h (models/ph_sac/rollouts._continuous_grid), h the model step 10 ms. Ported: testbed acrobot_swingup is environment/ph_sac/dmc/acrobot.py with its factory in common/ph_dmc/acrobot.py; the row builds, its task_* columns are checked against the factory, and tests/test_ph_dmc_*.py compare the port with dm_control (forward dynamics, reset law and open-loop trajectories; the reward is not dm_control's and is tested against its definition). Task values from docs/dmc_environments/dmc_environments.tex and docs/paper/sections/E_experiment_details.tex. dm_control acrobot/swingup (its plant, motor, reset and clock): two 1 m, 1 kg links (capsule radii 0.05 and 0.049 m), damping 0.05 on both hinges, elbow motor gear 2, torque +-2 N m; the model has no constraint to remove. 1 ms RK4 physics as the cart-pole port; fixed clock at dm_control's 10 ms control step (the reference period), 1000 decisions per 10 s episode. Reset: both angles uniform on [-pi, pi], velocities 0. Reward NOT dm_control's: dm_control's tol(|tip - target|; [0, 0.2], gaussian margin 1) is below 6e-4 whenever the tip is more than 2 m from the target, and no arm learned from it in 500k decisions; the reward of Zhang, Sathuluri and Zimmermann (2023), arXiv:2312.11311, Eq. 4, which replaced it on 2026-11-08, stayed flat near a mean rate of -0.085 with no upright in 40 runs (it remains reward kind zhang2023 of the port, but no row uses it). Since the second change of 2026-11-08 this row takes acrobot_xk-swingup's reward on this plant: the log-reciprocal of Xin and Kaneda's energy-and-elbow Lyapunov function without its elbow-rate term (X. Xin and M. Kaneda, Int. J. Robust Nonlinear Control 17(16):1503-1524, 2007, doi:10.1002/rnc.1184), r(s) = -log(max(V(s) / V_down, reward_floor)) with V = (E - upright_energy)^2 / 2 + lyapunov_k_p wrap(theta_2)^2 / 2 and V_down = energy_scale^2 / 2, E the mechanical energy of the port's chain (kinetic plus potential, zero with both links horizontal). The constants are this plant's, computed through the chain (environment/ph_sac/dmc/acrobot.py, acrobot_lyapunov_reward_terms; the environment reads them from this row and checks only that they are positive and finite): upright_energy = E at upright rest = b1 + b2 = 19.62 J and energy_scale = E(upright rest) - E(hanging rest) = 2 (b1 + b2) = 39.24 J, with b1 = g (m1 lc1 + m2 l1) = 14.715 N m and b2 = g m2 lc2 = 4.905 N m; lyapunov_k_p = 1.001 x Xin and Kaneda's lower bound (2/pi) min(b1^2, b2^2) = 15.3165, so 15.3318 (acrobot_xk's 61.2 against its bound 61.141 is the same ratio); reward_floor 1e-06 as acrobot_xk. Choices: the elbow is wrapped (|theta_2| <= pi) because the port's state is periodic, where acrobot_xk's elbow is unwrapped and capped at 4 pi by its failure set; no failure set is added, the log keeping runaway energies tame. The rate is state-only, 0 at hanging rest, at most -log(reward_floor) = 13.82 (upright at rest) and unbounded below, logarithmically in the energy, so the learned reward head stays linear (reward_rate_bounds None). No stop, no failure set. Decision box scaled to the motor: setpoint within +-1 rad, stiffness 0-20 N m/rad, damping 0-4 N m s/rad (k_max = 10 x 2 N m / 1 rad, damping 0.2 s x k_max, the rule that gives the cart-pole and Acrobot reference boxes at their +-10 limit), an elbow offset as acrobot_xk's; setpoint_error wrapped because both angles are periodic, wrapped observations here (acrobot_xk's unwrapped elbow served its travel limit, which dm_control lacks); flagged as a choice. Optional reward variant of acrobot-swingup (mode top), selected with --env-id acrobot-swingup --mode lyapunov_shoulder; every column equals that row's but env_reward_parameters and protocol_output_directory. Not a default: the top row keeps its reward. Not used in the final run (decided 2026-11-11). Reward: the top row's Lyapunov reward with a penalty on the unactuated shoulder, V_C = V + lyapunov_k_shoulder wrap(theta_1)^2 / 2 (theta_1 from upright), r = -log(max(V_C / V_C_down, reward_floor)) with V_C_down = energy_scale^2 / 2 + lyapunov_k_shoulder pi^2 / 2, V_C at hanging rest, so r = 0 there. V_C = 0 only at the upright at rest, so this variant asks for stabilization, where the top row's V = 0 on the whole set {E = upright_energy, theta_2 = 0} (the straight arm on its homoclinic orbit). No theory fixes the weight (Xin and Kaneda's bound covers only the elbow's k_P); the scale rule gives theta_1 = pi alone the cost energy_scale^2 / 2: lyapunov_k_shoulder = energy_scale^2 / pi^2 = 156.012 (environment/ph_sac/dmc/acrobot.py, acrobot_shoulder_weight), so V_C_down = energy_scale^2 = 1539.78.
